issue:
trace.mjs: traced() treats a git timeout as untraced, letting the edit through

`realGit.traced` (`plugins/trace/scripts/lib/trace.mjs`, the `traced(root)` adapter) checks the working tree for `.claude/trace.json`, then asks git whether `HEAD`, `origin/<default>` or `<default>` has it. Any error, including `out of time asking git and GitHub` from the per-call deadline, is caught and returns `false`.

So in a repository whose marker exists only in `HEAD` or on the default branch (for example, deleted or moved in the working tree), a slow git makes the hook treat it as untraced and let the edit, commit or PR through. Elsewhere the trace fails closed ("Failing open here would let an untraced edit, commit or PR through", `hook.mjs`).

Found by the spec review of #32. The behaviour predates #32.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When git cannot say whether the marker is in `HEAD` or the default branch, the edit, commit and PR gates refuse, naming the bypass, instead of treating the repository as untraced.
- [ ] A repository git positively says has no marker anywhere stays untraced, so untraced repositories are not gated.
- [ ] A test covers the timeout case.

**(a) Missing or partial**

> "When git cannot say whether the marker is in `HEAD` or the default branch, the edit, commit and PR gates refuse"

This is partial. `traced()` now lets errors through, but the `git()` helper it uses (`trace.mjs` ~768–772) still throws only on `r.error`, meaning a timeout or no git to run. Any non-zero exit returns `null`, which `traced()` reads as "no marker". I checked in $TMPDIR: every one of these exits 128, the same code as a real "no":
- path not in HEAD, rev not found, unborn HEAD (the genuine "no" cases);
- "detected dubious ownership";
- `.git/config` that won't parse;
- corrupt objects;
- `.git/HEAD` containing garbage.

So a repository whose marker is only in `HEAD` but that git refuses to read (for example, dubious ownership) is still treated as untraced, and the edit goes through. The same happens if git is killed by a signal other than the timeout (`status === null`, no `r.error`). The new comment, "Only git saying no makes a repository untraced", overstates what the code does. To tell them apart, the code could check the revision first with `rev-parse --verify -q <rev>^{tree}` (exit 1, no output, when it doesn't exist) and then `ls-tree <rev> -- .claude/trace.json` (exit 0 with empty output when the path is absent). - **`archive.mjs` shared deadline, new "could not be checked in time" denial, `hook.mjs` passing `world.timeLeft`, two archive tests:** none of this is needed for the acceptance criteria.
